detail: Newell suffered the toe injury in the Nov. 4 win over Washington and is now set to miss an extended period. With Mouhamed Gueye (foot) expected to miss at least three more weeks, Aaron Wiggins and Corey Kispert could see a slight bump in minutes moving forward.

Veesaar suffered the injury during a workout on Sept. 15, and an MRI confirmed the diagnosis. The No. 52 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Veesaar was expected to spend a lot of time with Atlanta's G League affiliate this season.

Neemias Queta should continue handling the bulk of Boston's center minutes, with Luka Garza and Chris Cenac potentially receiving additional opportunities. Robinson's next chance to return comes Sunday against the Spurs.

Allen has missed the Hornets' last four games, and the questionable tag suggests a decision on the availability of the veteran guard will be made closer to Saturday's 6 p.m. ET tipoff. Having Allen would allow the Hornets to deploy a reliable floor-stretching threat, as Allen is averaging 14.9 points per game while shooting 45.8 percent from three this season in his 13 regular-season contests.
Essengue should be able to play through a thumb sprain Saturday. He hasn't logged more than 15 minutes in any of his last 12 appearances, leaving Essengue with limited fantasy appeal.
Smith was spotted at practice Friday, per K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network. With the big man expected to play, fewer minutes will be on the table for Nic Claxton at center Saturday.

The rookie forward went down during Wednesday's loss to the Spurs, and he now needs surgery to repair a fractured right hand. More pressure will likely fall on Josh Giddey going forward, while the likes of Tre Jones and Isaac Okoro will have a chance for added streaming value.

Tomlin, who is recovering from a lower back stress reaction, has yet to suit up for the Cavs this season. He continues to get ruled out 24 hours in advance of tipoff, indicating he's still not close, so he can be viewed as week-to-week moving forward.

Cunningham won't suit up Friday and will miss a second straight game, and the third of his last five, while dealing with right knee tendinopathy. This means Daniss Jenkins should run the point for Detroit on Friday, while Isaiah Joe could be in line for another start at shooting guard. Cunningham's next chance to return will come Sunday against the Magic.

Santos lasted just eight minutes in the game, posting five points (2-4 FG, 1-1 3Pt), two rebounds and a steal while coming off the bench. Further tests will be needed to determine the severity of the injury, but for the time being, he should be considered questionable to face the Clippers on Sunday.

Curry has already missed each of Golden State's last six contests after suffering an oblique abdominal tear Nov. 11, and he won't be given the green light to return anytime in the immediate future. De'Anthony Melton is expected to continue working as the Warriors' starting point guard in the meantime, with LJ Cryer and Brandon Williams also getting more minutes.

Porzingis said he was looking forward to joining the Warriors, but his body didn't respond the way he wanted it too during his ramp-up process before the season. Additionally, he said he will work with the Warriors on a solution that "makes sense." Porzingis is making this decision to prioritize his health and will hopefully turn a corner soon on that front.

The veteran center is in danger of sitting out for the first time since Nov. 16 in Miami. If Adams doesn't play, Clint Capela would likely have the backup center position all to himself behind Alperen Sengun on Saturday.

McConnell will miss a third consecutive game Friday as he continues to manage a sore left hamstring. His next chance to return will come Saturday in the second leg of this back-to-back set; meanwhile, Quenton Jackson should continue to pick up additional minutes off the bench.

Sheppard required a full repair and is without a definitive timetable for a return to action. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) expected to miss at least two weeks, Quenton Jackson figures to see a significant uptick in playing time. Two-way player Braden Smith could also see increased action with the parent club.

Niederhauser suffered the injury on the same foot he previously had surgery on, so it's clear the Clippers are being overly cautious. The big man finished the game with two points (1-3 FG, 0-1 FT) and a block in 10 minutes off the bench. The Clippers play again Sunday on the road against the Warriors.

Jakucionis will miss his second game of the season due to left ankle tenosynovitis. In his absence, Ryan Rollins, Caris LeVert and AJ Green could see expanded roles, while rookie Brayden Burries should also get a slight bump in minutes.

With Ball and Anthony Edwards (knee) sidelined, Ayo Dosunmu and Bones Hyland should handle increased ball-handling responsibilities. Minnesota's depleted backcourt could also create additional scoring opportunities for Jaden McDaniels. Ball's next opportunity to return comes Monday against Sacramento.

Reese dropped a 15-point, 15-rebound double-double in the Squadron's win over the Mexico City Capitanes on Saturday and will return to the parent club ahead of its game Monday. Through five regular-season appearances at the NBA level this season, the big man is averaging 1.2 points and 1.0 rebounds in 5.4 minutes per tilt.

This was the expectation after the star guard requested a trade from the Pelicans earlier Friday. Given his standing with the club, Murray can be tentatively considered doubtful for future contests while New Orleans tries to find him another home.

Once Sorber begins on-court work, there will be a ramp-up period before he's cleared for game-time action, so his absence will likely extend well beyond this initial 6-8-week window. Sorber was selected by the Thunder with the No. 15 pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, but he missed his entire rookie season after tearing the ACL in his right knee and has yet to play this season due to right knee issues.

This is another massive blow to an Oklahoma City squad that's already set to be without Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) for most, if not all, of the season. With Holmgren sidelined, Kenrich Williams, Jaylin Williams and Aday Mara are all candidates to see increased playing time. Two-way player Brooks Barnhizer could also see more minutes.

Porter signed with the Magic on Nov. 25, so it's understandable that he'll need some time to get into playing shape. His next chance to play will come Sunday at Detroit on the second leg of a back-to-back set.
Black is a candidate to miss the first half of this back-to-back set. Tristan da Silva would likely enter the starting lineup for the Magic on Saturday if Black sits out.

Wade was added to the injury report earlier Friday due to injury management of a hamstring problem, and in the end, the forward has been ruled out. This poses a problem for the 76ers, as Jaylen Brown (hamstring) is out as well. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope could be in line for a bigger role because of the absences. Wade's next chance to play will come Saturday against the Rockets on the second leg of a back-to-back set.

James will sit out the second leg of this back-to-back set after impressing in Friday's win over the Pacers, tallying 21 points (8-13 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 3-4 FT), seven rebounds, six assists and a block over 27 minutes. Dean Wade (hamstring) is questionable, while Joel Embiid (foot) and Jaylen Brown (hamstring) are out, so the 76ers will be depleted Saturday. Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe will have bigger roles on offense, while Jabari Walker, Dominick Barlow and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope will all see more minutes with James on the shelf.

Brown's absence from the road trip means he won't play against the Pacers on Friday or against the Rockets on Saturday. However, the star forward might be able to return for Tuesday's matchup against the Grizzlies. With Brown out, Dean Wade (hamstring), Jabari Walker and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope are all options to see more playing time at small forward.

Krejci suffered the ankle injury in last Wednesday's win over the Suns and is set to miss an extended period after undergoing surgery. With the 26-year-old and Ja Morant (hamstring) both on the shelf, Jrue Holiday and Sidy Cissoko should continue seeing increased minutes.

Bamba will officially sit out Friday's contest after waking up feeling under the weather. Jaxson Hayes (knee) and Jusuf Nurkic (foot) are both available to face Denver and figure to absorb Bamba's playing time.

Beekman is set for an extended absence, with his re-evaluation timeline suggesting he could remain sidelined beyond the initial three-week window. The injury further limits Washington's backcourt depth, though Beekman's absence is unlikely to have a significant impact on standard fantasy leagues.
